title: Owned exact polynomial factorization resources
objective: Replace packed capacity-retry factorization of ZZ[x] and QQ[x] with generated callee-owned FLINT factorization resources that compute once, expose unit factors and exponents safely, preserve Sage semantics and portable fallback behavior, and require no operation-specific compiler changes

oracles: existing ordinary-Python and Sage-compatible factorization semantics
exceptions: This coherent migration spans declarations, generated resource ownership, public polynomial routing, lifecycle tests, and performance ratchets; splitting it would leave an unverified partial ABI.

handoff.summary: ZZ[x] and QQ[x] now factor once into a generated callee-owned ExactPolynomialFactorization resource. Public Node factorization queries the unit, exponents, and factor count as scalars, copies each variable-size FLINT factor directly into an independent sealed polynomial resource, and closes the owner in finally; it never materializes packed compatibility storage, chooses a uniform limb capacity, retries computation, loops over coefficients, or calls legacy N-API. Existing packed factorization remains the tested portable capability fallback. Focused tests cover public and direct generated adapters, native-disabled and forced-portable execution, constants and zero, 65,537-bit skew, owner/factor lifetime independence, wrong/closed resources, injected failures, idempotent close, external-memory accounting, and ASan/UBSan lifecycle fuzzing. A five-sample skew benchmark measured 2.59 ms median over ZZ and 3.29 ms over QQ on this host, and the repository polynomial performance budget gained a ZZ factorization ratchet.
risks: The new owned factorization declaration is currently wasm=False; browser execution deliberately retains the existing packed declared-FLINT fallback until generated resource ownership has a Wasm host adapter.
Physical retained-size accounting reads the pinned FLINT fmpz_poly_factor layout, so a future FLINT ABI upgrade must revalidate the accounting header and sanitizer harness.
Only linux-x64 was exercised locally; generated declarations preserve the required Windows, macOS, and arm64 policy, whose CI remains the platform oracle.
next_steps: Independently review generated ownership, retained-size accounting, and Sage-compatible unit normalization before integration.
Add generated Wasm lowering for owned factorization resources, then route the portable browser path through the same callee-owned protocol when supported.
Keep packed exact factorization only as the explicit portable interchange fallback; remove it once every supported host can own generated FLINT resources.
